items.text: Among adults aged 70 and over discharged alive from the medical wards, is an anticholinergic burden score of 3 or more at discharge, compared with 0 to 2, associated with a first injurious fall within 90 days after adjustment for frailty and indication?
items.population: Adults aged 70 and over discharged alive from the medical wards, first eligible discharge per patient
items.intervention: Anticholinergic burden score of 3 or more at discharge (exposure)
items.outcome: First emergency visit or admission coded for a fall with injury
items.setting: 450-bed teaching hospital with regional admission data from three public hospitals

items.text: Is any association concentrated in patients who started an anticholinergic medicine during the admission, within the first 30 days after discharge?
items.population: Same cohort, restricted to new users and to users with no anticholinergic medicine before admission
items.intervention: Anticholinergic medicine started during the admission
items.comparator: No anticholinergic medicine at admission or discharge

finer: Feasible from existing dispensing and admission data within about 40 analyst hours; interesting to pharmacy and geriatric medicine; novel for the post-discharge window; ethical as secondary use with a waiver request; relevant because it decides routine pharmacist workload.
summary: One primary PECO question and one pre-specified new-user question.
